text:
ops-bot: ALERT: prod-edge-us-west2 - spike in 502/connection resets from LB -> backends (see svc=edge-proxy), 2026-03-18T09:02:03Z
Sam_infra: seeing same in Grafana, error rate jumped ~8x around 09:00 UTC
Jess: rolling back any infra changes? I applied a small Terraform change to vpc/nacl rules at 08:58 for tightening access to an onboarding subnet
Sam_infra: that could be it. What exactly changed?
Jess: removed an overly-broad ingress rule and added explicit source ranges. snippet: ```resource "aws_network_acl_rule" "edge_ingress" {
  rule_number = 100
  egress      = false
  protocol    = "-1"
  rule_action = "allow"
  cidr_block  = "10.0.0.0/16" # <-- replaced 0.0.0.0/0 previously
}```
Rui: aha — NACLs are stateless. If you restrict inbound to only the front-end CIDR but didn't allow ephemeral ports in the outbound/egress rules, return traffic from backends to LB can be dropped.
Aisha: confirmed on a host in the affected AZ: tcpdump on eth0 shows SYNs to LB reach the pod, but responses fail with "ICMP port unreachable" from the NAT subnets.
Devon: quick check: can you dump one of the NACLs? `aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-abc123`
Jess: posted the acl JSON to the #eng-infra-private gist (link) — outbound rules only allowed destination ports 80,443, and blocked others. I thought SGs would cover it but NACLs are before SGs.
Sam_infra: right — NACLs are evaluated first. If ephemeral outbound ports (1024-65535) are blocked for egress from the subnet where the LB lives, the TCP handshake can't be completed.
Rui: fix options: (1) widen NACL egress to allow 1024-65535 to the backend CIDR, (2) relax the ingress source range back to 0.0.0.0/0 for the LB subnet and rely on SGs, or (3) add explicit stateful NAT mapping rules.
Aisha: for fast mitigation I'd allow ephemeral range out from the LB subnets. I can apply a 1-line TF change and plan+apply. Thoughts? :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Jess: +1 do that. I'll pause any other network PRs.
Devon: while you're applying, I'm toggling healthcheck to slower and enabling fallback route to us-east for critical traffic.
Sam_infra: log of the workaround: `aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0abc --egress --rule-number 65000 --protocol -1 --rule-action allow --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0` (we added ephemeral allow with a high rule number)
ops-bot: NOTE: Terraform plan applied by jess (deploy-id: tf-2026-03-18-0922)
Jess: applied the short-term rule to allow 1024-65535 egress from edge subnets. Monitoring now.
Aisha: error rate dropping back to baseline over the last 4 minutes, 502s down from 7% to 0.6%
Sam_infra: solid. Follow-up: we need a postmortem step to update our NACL policy doc and add a pre-merge guard to detect removing ephemeral-port egress rules for LB subnets.
Rui: I'll add a check in the terraform pipeline: fail if NACL changes remove ephemeral-port egress in any edge subnets.
Jess: and I'll open a PR to move to SG-first model where possible so we don't accidentally break stateful flows with NACLs again.
Devon: thumbs up :thumbsup: — marking incident as mitigated, will leave thread open for follow-ups.
